content:
The terms and conditions for Apple Cash have just been updated, and Apple is notifying users of two changes that will soon take effect.

Apple Cash will begin requiring users to verify their identity in order to add funds to their balance, and may also enable "externally initiated funds transactions."

If you use Apple Cash, you may have just received an email, or will soon receive one, notifying you of changes to the service's terms and conditions.

Apple partners with Green Dot Bank to provide Apple Cash, and the bank's revised terms page (available here) contains several important changes, which Apple specifically mentions in the email.

The first relates to identity verification. According to Apple:

Another upcoming change involves "externally initiated funds transactions." Although no firm date has been set, the new terms give Green Dot the ability to offer that feature. Apple writes:

The only other change Apple highlights in the email concerns the arbitration section of Green Dot's terms. Aside from Apple encouraging users to review the changes carefully, no specific updates are mentioned, as the changes relate to user rights and the procedures for handling disputes.

Have you spotted any other changes in the revised Apple Cash terms? Let us know in the comments.
